eval_instructions: Run these evals against approved test agents or minimal fixtures; mock administrative writes in fixtures. This skill is additive and reversible: it copies one guard file, wires an INPUT gate before the LLM and optional output auditing before the reply, preserves existing configuration, and guides the Graph permission grant + DLP policy choice. Delegated agents use their own agentic token at /me with Content.Process.User; Node.js client-secret FMI S2S agents use the agent identity token at /users/{sponsor}/... with Content.Process.All. Never use a blueprint app-only token or admin-consent on the blueprint. Verify contentEntry.name, fail-closed defaults, matching language/authentication, and the new / existing / skip policy choice. The supplied policy blocks inputs, not generated responses. Stop before copying into a plain bot without supported authentication.

trigger_tests.instructions: Run each prompt in a fresh session with the full agent365 skill library loaded. should_trigger prompts must activate purview-dlp-integration. should_not_trigger prompts must activate the named sibling (or no skill) and must NOT activate purview-dlp-integration — they guard the DLP-vs-observability/tools boundary. Report hit rate in each direction (>=2 runs each).

evals.prompt: Add Purview DLP to my A365 agent and block credit card numbers before the LLM
evals.description: Node.js @microsoft/agents-hosting agent with a365.config.json + a365.generated.config.json present; user wants a new DLP policy.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Node.js, reads the a365 config for app id/display name/blueprint id, copies assets/purview.ts next to the agent class, applies the wiring snippet (INPUT gate before the LLM, OUTPUT gate before the reply) passing this.authorization, appends PURVIEW_DLP_ENABLED=true to .env, guides Grant-DelegatedGraphScope.ps1 to append Content.Process.User, asks which policy to use and (default) runs New-AiAppDlpPolicy.ps1, then explains the [purview] BLOCKED verify log.
expectations: Step 0: Detects Node.js/TypeScript via package.json (@microsoft/agents-hosting)
Before-you-start: Reads a365.config.json / a365.generated.config.json for app id, display name, blueprint id, and current Graph scopes
Step 2: Copies assets/purview.ts (the guard) into the agent source unchanged
Step 3: Wires the INPUT gate before the LLM call and the OUTPUT gate before the reply, passing this.authorization + turn context
Step 4: Appends PURVIEW_DLP_ENABLED=true to .env
Step 5: Runs Grant-DelegatedGraphScope.ps1 to APPEND Content.Process.User (never az ad app permission admin-consent on the blueprint app)
Step 6: Asks new / existing / skip, then runs New-AiAppDlpPolicy.ps1 for the new policy (default SIT Credit Card Number)
Constraints: Uses the agentic delegated token evaluated as /me; always sets contentEntry.name; fails closed by default
Step 8: Verifies with a Luhn-valid test value and judges success by the [purview] uploadText -> BLOCKED (errors=0) log, not DistributionStatus

evals.prompt: Add data loss prevention to this Python agent using my existing 'Corp PII' policy
evals.description: Python microsoft-agents-hosting-core agent; user already has a DLP policy and does NOT want a new one.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects Python, copies assets/purview.py, wires evaluate_prompt/evaluate_response passing auth, auth_handler_name, and context, appends the env vars, and for the existing-policy path runs New-AiAppDlpPolicy.ps1 -ListExisting to confirm the app id is covered — creating nothing new. It does not create a new policy.
expectations: Step 0: Detects Python via pyproject.toml / requirements.txt (microsoft-agents-hosting-*)
Step 2: Copies assets/purview.py (the guard) into the agent source
Step 3: Wires the gates in process_user_message passing auth, auth_handler_name, context (already handler parameters)
Step 3: Confirms the caller sends returned block/withhold text; a host on_message callback must instead await context.send_activity(...) before returning
Step 6 Option B: Runs ./New-AiAppDlpPolicy.ps1 -ListExisting and checks whether the chosen policy COVERS THIS APP
Step 6 Option B: If the policy already covers the app id, creates nothing and confirms Mode=Enable + a RestrictAccess/Block rule on UploadText
Does NOT create a new DLP policy
Constraints: agentic delegated token via authorization.exchange_token(...); fail-closed default

evals.prompt: Wire a Purview DLP gate into my .NET agent but I'll add the policy myself later
evals.description: .NET Microsoft.Agents.* agent; user chooses to skip policy creation (Option C).
evals.expected_output: The skill detects .NET, warns the .NET guard is a best-effort port, copies assets/purview.cs, wires OnMessageAsync (PurviewGuard.Instance.EvaluatePromptAsync/EvaluateResponseAsync passing UserAuthorization + agentic handler name + turnContext), sets PURVIEW_DLP_ENABLED in the process environment or selected launchSettings.json profile, and for Option C creates no policy — explaining the guard stays enabled but logs 'allowed ... 0 policyAction(s)' until the user adds a matching Applications/Managed-cloud-apps policy with a RestrictAccess=Block rule and EnforcementPlanes=Application.
expectations: Step 0: Detects .NET via *.csproj (Microsoft.Agents.*) and flags the .NET guard as best-effort (verify ITurnContext / UserAuthorization namespaces)
Step 2: Copies assets/purview.cs into the agent source
Step 2: The guard uses the runtime agent identity for agents[0].identifier when available, preserving the configured blueprintId and policy applicationLocation
Step 3: Wires OnMessageAsync passing UserAuthorization, the agentic auth handler name, and turnContext
Step 4: Enables the guard through process environment variables or the selected launchSettings.json profile, not appsettings.json or an unloaded .env file
Step 6 Option C: Creates no policy; explains the guard logs 'allowed ... 0 policyAction(s)' until a matching policy exists
Step 6 Option C: Lists the 6 required policy properties (Applications location, EnforcementPlanes=Application, SIT condition, RestrictAccess=Block on UploadText, Mode=Enable, optional notify)
Constraints: Never runs az ad app permission admin-consent on the blueprint app
Marks best-effort wiring with the A365 DLP best-effort comment

evals.prompt: Block sensitive data in my agent — it's a plain Node.js bot, not provisioned with Agent 365 yet
evals.description: Plain Node.js bot with no A365 config, supported agentic hosting/authentication, or existing client-secret FMI path.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the missing supported authentication path and stops before copying or wiring the guard. It explains that manually supplied app IDs cannot provide authentication and routes to a365-setup; integration can resume after the prerequisites are satisfied.
expectations: Before-you-start: Detects there is no a365.config.json / a365.generated.config.json
Step 1: Confirms no supported agentic delegated or Node.js client-secret FMI authentication path is present
Step 1: Stops before guard copying, handler edits, permission grants, or policy creation and routes to a365-setup
Does not treat manually supplied app IDs as a substitute for hosting/authentication
Does not fabricate an app id or blueprint id

evals.prompt: Add Purview DLP to my Node.js S2S worker using its existing client-secret FMI authentication and my existing AI-app policy
evals.description: Node.js worker without AgentApplication; canonical AGENT365_* client-secret FMI settings and a sponsor user ID are already configured.
evals.expected_output: The skill selects assets/purview-s2s.ts, wires evaluatePrompt(text) before the LLM and optional evaluateResponse(text) for output audit, and guides Grant-ContentProcessAppRole.ps1 for the agent identity. It verifies the existing policy instead of creating one and preserves the current authentication.
expectations: Step 0: Selects the Node.js S2S guard rather than the delegated purview.ts guard
Step 3: Calls evaluatePrompt(text) / evaluateResponse(text) without TurnContext or Authorization arguments
Step 4: Confirms AGENT365_TENANT_ID, AGENT365_AGENT_ID, AGENT365_CLIENT_ID, AGENT365_CLIENT_SECRET, and PURVIEW_SPONSOR_USER_ID without exposing secrets
Step 5: Uses Grant-ContentProcessAppRole.ps1 for Content.Process.All on the agent identity SP; skips the delegated grant script
Step 6: Verifies the existing Applications policy covers the app and blocks UploadText; creates no new policy
Constraints: Uses the agent identity FMI token at /users/{sponsor}/..., never a blueprint app-only token or /me
Constraints: Does not promise response filtering or switch managed-identity-only agents to client-secret authentication
